Name: Creative Business Cup
Quick info: Creative Business Network global competition for creative-industry startups. National rounds (incl. Denmark) feed Global Finals. Prize and in-kind packages vary by year and national partner. Incorporated startups often preferred for competition rounds.

Name: EY Entrepreneur of the Year
Quick info: Prestigious annual award programme recognising outstanding Danish entrepreneurs across categories; visibility and national profile.

Name: Global Startup Awards
Quick info: International startup awards with Nordic regional rounds celebrating founders across categories and stages.

Name: Green Leap Challenge
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Food & Agriculture, Cleantech & Energy
Quick info: Food & Bio Cluster Denmark annual idea competition for green agrifood and bioresource concepts (often pre-sales). Typically 3 × DKK 50K prizes plus exposure. Watch Food & Bio Cluster news/events for the next call. Winners typically incorporate or already have CVR to receive DKK 50K.

Name: Nordic Proptech Awards 2026
Quick info: Annual awards recognising leading Nordic proptech startups and innovations in real estate technology.

Name: Nordic Women in Tech Awards
Quick info: Volunteer-run annual awards gala celebrating female role models in Nordic tech across 11 categories; conference and networking events.

Name: Odin Award
Quick info: Odense/Fyn awards (Odin, Tech, Concept, Impact) organised with Ignite Odense / Coworking Plus. Main prize historically around DKK 40K; category amounts vary. Concept targets early pre-company ideas; other categories favour established startups. Concept category targets pre-CVR ideas; Odin/Tech/Impact categories are for established startups (CVR expected).

Name: CPH Townhall
Quick info: Townhall-style Copenhagen startup community events run under Techstartup.dk (pitches, networking, ecosystem updates). Townhall is one of their recurring formats.

Name: Danmarks Entreprenørskabsfestival
Criteria: Pupils, students and educators in entrepreneurship education (primary to higher ed)
Quick info: Fonden for Entreprenørskab’s national entrepreneurship-in-education festival across six locations (primary, youth and higher education). Includes INSPIRE teacher conference, pitching finales (e.g. Projekt Edison, Start Up Programme) and prizes — primarily an education ecosystem event, not a general startup conference.

Name: Digital Tech Summit
Quick info: Major Danish tech conference connecting startups, corporates, and investors with programme tracks across digital technologies.

Name: Founder Festival
Criteria: Self-employed / sole traders / aspiring founders (Odense focus)
Quick info: One-day Founders Festival in Odense (Thrige Firkanten), organised by Ejendomsselskabet Olav de Linde and Odense Kommune. Talks, workshops and 1:1 advisor sessions for new and established self-employed founders and people considering starting.

Name: Ignite
Quick info: Odense entrepreneurship festival (Ignite Odense) with talks, networking, and award ceremonies for Funen-region startups.

Name: JoinUp North
Quick info: Annual Nordic startup gathering connecting founders, investors, and ecosystem players across the region. Cross-border networking and matchmaking — no funding attached.

Name: Nordic Fintech Week
Quick info: Annual fintech conference and networking week for Nordic fintech startups, investors, and financial institutions. Programme tracks, panels, and investor meetings across the Nordic ecosystem.

Name: Nordic Innovation Fair
Quick info: Fall innovation fair showcasing Nordic startups, research, and cross-border collaboration opportunities.

Name: Odense Investor Summit
Quick info: Annual investor–startup summit in Odense connecting Funen-region companies with angels, VCs, and corporates. Pitching and curated matchmaking for the local growth ecosystem.

Name: SMIL
Quick info: Annual Aarhus startup festival curated by Startup Aarhus (next edition marketed as SMIL’27). Curated sessions connecting founders, investors and operators — not a cash-prize competition.

Name: Seedster
Quick info: Week-long entrepreneurship bootcamp in Marbella (not a pitch competition). Mentorship, workshops, and networking; fee covers programme, catering, and hotel.

Name: Startup Aarhus Townhall
Quick info: Aarhus startup townhall events with local founder pitches, ecosystem news, and networking.

Name: Startup Lab
Quick info: Copenhagen startup community and event series offering networking, pitch opportunities, and ecosystem connections for early-stage founders.

Name: Startup Planet
Quick info: Danish startup community event series for networking, inspiration, and founder connections.

Name: TechBBQ
Quick info: Nordic's major tech conference in Copenhagen: investor meetings, side events, and startup showcase.

Name: Even Founders
Quick info: Non-profit supporting Nordic women founders via Startup School (12-week programme), investor database, co-founder matchmaking, and ecosystem partnerships. Tuborgfondet-backed.

Name: Found Diverse
Quick info: Non-profit promoting diversity in Danish entrepreneurship through events, mentoring, and community programmes (founded from NWiTA alumni network).

Name: Intech Founders
Quick info: Community and programme for female-led tech startups in Denmark with networking, mentoring, and founder support events.

Name: Kvinde kompagniet
Quick info: Danish network for female entrepreneurs offering peer community, events, and business sparring.

Name: Ladies First
Quick info: Copenhagen-based community supporting female founders with networking events, workshops, and mentorship.

Name: Next Women
Quick info: Nordic network and platform for female-led startups with events, visibility, and investor connections across the region.

Name: Nordic Female Founders
Quick info: Nordic community connecting female founders with mentors, investors, and cross-border networking opportunities.

Name: Nordic Women’s Health Hub
Quick info: Nordic Women’s Health community/hub supporting women’s health innovation and female founders with network, visibility and sector programmes across the Nordics.

Name: Women in Front
Quick info: Network for Danish female leaders and entrepreneurs with events, mentorship, and leadership development.

Name: Women in Tech
Quick info: Danish community promoting women in technology through events, mentoring, role models, and career support.

Name: Akademikernes Startup
Quick info: Member benefit from Akademikernes A-kasse: 3-month Copenhagen incubator, online incubator, and on-demand courses with mentoring and networking. Open to members exploring entrepreneurship, including while on dagpenge.

Name: BII Bio Studio
Criteria: Principal Investigator (prof/assoc prof, 3+ years as independent group leader); challenge-call scoped; pre-commercial project with no existing company or external investment
Funding Amount: Up to DKK 5.35M/year for up to 3 years (in-kind; convertible loan in year 3)
Quick info: Company-creation programme for academic researchers. Highly selective multi-step process (expression of interest, scientific pitch, diligence). BII encourages early dialogue on project fit before applying. Project team is hired at BII; Entrepreneur-in-Residence leads company formation (spin-out typically around year 2). Thematic calls in Human Health, Planetary Health, and related focus areas. TRL 2–4. Company-creation for entrepreneurial academic PIs; multi-year funding.

Name: BII Quantum Lab
Criteria: Early-stage startup HQ in NATO country; dual-use quantum technology addressing NATO DIANA challenge areas
Segment tags: Quantum Tech, Defense Tech, Deep Tech
Quick info: 6-month programme (formerly Deep Tech Lab – Quantum), run with NATO DIANA. Supports dual-use quantum technologies with both civilian and defence applications. Access to NATO-wide defence, security, and resilience networks. TRL early (quantum startups). Early-stage quantum startups (BII / NATO DIANA collaboration context).

Name: BII Upscalator
Criteria: Biosolutions company with validated technology and core R&D completed, where further progress depends on scaling; no commercial investment or for-profit financing; core IP owned by, exclusively licensed to, or clearly licensable to the company
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Food & Agriculture, Cleantech & Energy
Funding Amount: Convertible loan of DKK 3–5M per project (milestone-based tranches)
Deadline: Up to four decision cycles per year (next: 1 September 2026, 14:00 CEST)
Quick info: BII programme helping biosolutions companies move validated concepts toward production at scale. Provides a dedicated BII anchor plus access to BII's community, network, fundraising platform and events. Requires a team with the technical, operational and commercial capability to execute the scale-up.

Name: BII Venture Lab
Criteria: Early-stage life science or deep tech startup; Danish CVR required for funding; prioritises Danish HQ, operations, and leadership
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Deep Tech, Cleantech & Energy
Quick info: 12-month accelerator maturing science and business readiness. Open-call programme for incorporated startups in Human Health, Planetary Health, and Quantum. May apply before CVR exists if a clear plan to establish a Danish entity before programme start. Eligible Danish teams may later apply for Venture House follow-on (DKK 10.5M). TRL 3–5. Early-stage life science & deep tech; founder-friendly convertible funding.

Name: BII Venture House
Criteria: Exclusive follow-on for BII Venture Lab alumni headquartered and operating with leadership in Denmark; active Venture Lab participation required.
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Deep Tech, Cleantech & Energy
Deadline: By invitation / Venture Lab progress (not open call)
Quick info: BII follow-on programme after Venture Lab. Founder-friendly convertible loan and continued BII support to mature toward Series A readiness. Distinct from BII Upscalator, which is a separate biosolutions scale-up initiative.

Name: Beta Health
Quick info: National hospital innovation platform (Novo Nordisk Foundation). Clinicians/researchers at Danish public hospitals apply for BETA.05 (DKK 500K) or BETA.10 (DKK 1M) grants plus structured accelerator support.

Name: Beyond Beta
Criteria: DK-based startups; CVR max 7 years; MVP or customers
Quick info: EU-funded 12-month national accelerator run by Accelerace, industry clusters, and Danish Business Hubs. Tailored mentoring, workshops, and investor access. Free to join.

Name: CBS CSE (Copenhagen School of Entrepreneurship)
Criteria: Students, recent graduates, or researchers at Danish higher-ed institutions; startup or committed idea stage
Quick info: CBS entrepreneurship centre (distinct from former UCPH CSE/Venture Cup). Incubator and accelerator for founders at idea through growth stage; EXPLORE pre-incubation, Deep Green Innovators, and OpenInnovation with DTU Skylab and KU Actory.

Name: Canute
Quick info: Scaling advisory and accelerator (now Canute by Thursday). Helps Danish founders enter US, UK, and Germany with market-entry programmes, fundraising strategy, and public-funding support. Scaling programmes assume an incorporated Danish startup.

Name: Care Tech Challenge
Criteria: DK startups 0–3 years old (CVR); limited commercial revenue on the solution
Funding Amount: No cash grant (accelerator + exposure; Danish.Care membership fee)
Quick info: Danish.Care CareTech CHALLENGE accelerator for assistive/welfare-tech startups. Activities include pitches, Investor Day, Health & Rehab exhibition, workshops and industry matchmaking. Participation requires screening plus paid Danish.Care membership (Group 1). Company age 0–3 years based on CVR.

Name: Climate-KIC Urban Mobility Food
Criteria: EU-based urban mobility or food systems startups
Quick info: EIT Climate-KIC programmes for EU startups in urban mobility and sustainable food systems. Access to innovation programmes, pilots, and European cleantech networks.

Name: DIF Innovation Lab
Quick info: DIF (Danish sports federation) innovation lab bridging sportstech startups with federations, clubs, athletes, and universities for user testing and scaling. SportsTech Denmark membership and government-funded innovation packages available.

Name: Defence Tech Denmark
Criteria: DK-based defense or security tech startups
Quick info: Community and support network for Danish defence and dual-use security startups, linking founders with defence stakeholders, testing opportunities, and ecosystem partners.

Name: EESA
Quick info: Energy and sustainability accelerator/community supporting Danish cleantech startups with mentoring, industry connections, and programme activities in the green transition.

Name: Food and Bio Cluster
Quick info: Danish cluster organisation for food, bio, and agri-tech companies offering networking, internationalisation support, innovation projects, and sector-specific programmes.

Name: Founder to Leader
Quick info: Leadership development programme for Danish startup founders focusing on management skills, team building, and scaling as a CEO. Programme targets founders with an operating company.

Name: Future Manufacturers
Quick info: Manufacturing and industry 4.0 startup programme supporting Danish production-tech founders with sector expertise and scaling support.

Name: Game Hub
Criteria: DK-based gaming or interactive media startups
Quick info: Danish games industry hub offering community, events, mentoring, and business development for gaming and interactive media startups.

Name: Hub for Innovation in Tourism
Funding Amount: Programme support (accelerator; not a fixed cash grant)
Quick info: National Hub for Innovation in Tourism (HIT) — partnership of Dansk Kyst- og Naturturisme, MeetDenmark and Dansk Storbyturisme. Startup accelerator, matchmaking and network for tourism-relevant founders; co-funded by ESF+ and Danmarks Erhvervsfremmebestyrelse.

Name: Ideas Lab
Criteria: Promising startups/talent in games, film, XR, animation (Aarhus)
Quick info: Filmby Aarhus incubator / startup office (Ideas Lab) for digital creative ventures in games, film, XR and animation. Office space, mentoring, legal/accountant access, workshops and masterclasses toward acceleration — no standard cash grant.

Name: Incuba
Quick info: Danish incubator supporting early-stage tech startups with workspace, mentoring, and business development in Aalborg/North Denmark region.

Name: Leap Forward
Quick info: Tech startup growth programme offering mentoring and scaling support for Danish early-stage companies.

Name: Lighthouse Launch
Criteria: UCPH students, researchers, and postdocs with a concrete idea; KU affiliation required
Quick info: KU Lighthouse 14-week pre-accelerator for evidence-based idea validation through structured experiments. Open to students, researchers, and postdocs; replaces the former KU–Accelerace cohort pathway. Mentoring and workshops; prepares teams for POC funding, accelerators, or investment.

Name: Maritime Stars
Quick info: Maritime tech startup programme in Denmark connecting founders with shipping, offshore, and port industry partners for pilots and commercialisation.

Name: Neighborhood
Quick info: Community-driven startup hub in Copenhagen supporting local, impact-oriented founders with workspace, events, and peer network.

Name: Odense Robotics Startup Fund
Quick info: Odense Robotics cluster support for Danish robotics, automation, and drone startups including mentoring, investor access, and internationalisation via cluster programmes.

Name: Open Entrepreneurship
Criteria: Researchers at Danish universities with research-based commercialisation potential
Quick info: National collaboration across all eight Danish universities connecting researchers with experienced entrepreneurs and investors. No direct grant funding. A flagship activity is the Co-founder Run (twice yearly): a nationwide matching process that helps research-based pre-startup teams find commercial co-founders. Also offers investor matchmaking, E-corps, and support across Deep Tech, Life Sciences, Digital, and SHAPE. Gateway to pathways such as Innoexplorer and spin-out formation.
KU contact hint: KU Lighthouse / OE at UCPH; central unit DTU

Name: PreFlight
Quick info: Nordic pre-seed programme helping very early startups validate ideas, build MVPs, and prepare for first funding rounds.

Name: SPARK Denmark
Criteria: Health/life science projects with clinical or commercial potential
Funding Amount: Up to 700,000 DKK (350,000 DKK per year)
Quick info: 2×12-month structured mentoring; funds proof-of-concept studies, consultants, and prototyping only. Funds proof-of-concept work for researchers; not for established companies. TRL low (academic PoC). Life-science mentoring + up to DKK 700K PoC funding.

Name: STEAR
Quick info: Danish tech startup support programme offering mentoring and ecosystem access for early-stage founders.

Name: Soundtech
Criteria: DK-based audio or music tech startups
Quick info: Audio and music technology incubator/community in Denmark for startups developing sound, music, and media-tech products.

Name: Tech Nordic
Quick info: Nordic tech startup community and support network for early-stage companies seeking cross-border connections and growth resources.

Name: The Circular Lab
Quick info: Ecoembes TheCircularLab GoCircular: European open-innovation community for circular-economy startups. Visibility via goCircular Radar, networking, challenges and GoCircularPass certification. Open to European startups (including Nordics); not a classic DK cash grant.

Name: Time to Raise
Criteria: Founder-led startups currently fundraising or fundraising within ~6 months
Quick info: Techarena fundraising accelerator for founder-led companies (not women-only). Focuses on investor readiness, warm intros and raising capital faster; alumni report capital raised via the programme.

Name: We Build Denmark
Quick info: Construction and built-environment innovation cluster programme; annual activities for cleantech and construction startups.

Name: IBIS (Initiative for Biofertilizer Innovation and Science)
Criteria: Open Innovation in Science calls; universities/public research + collaborators (Global North & South)
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Food & Agriculture, Cleantech & Energy
Funding Amount: OIS project calls within DKK 215M platform (NNF + Gates Foundation)
Deadline: Calls announced via IBIS / NNF (check ibis.dtu.dk)
Quick info: Global biofertiliser R&D initiative hosted at DTU Bioengineering; UCPH is a partner. Open, non-GMO, no patents on organisms/use. Builds discovery-to-field pipeline. TRL: low–mid (foundational research through field-testing).
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk
KU contact hint: Preaward RSO (primary). IBIS Secretariat, DTU Bioengineering.

Name: Lundbeck Frontier
Criteria: Academic teams working on early-stage neuroscience discoveries
Quick info: Focus: psychiatry, neurodegeneration, CNS drug discovery. Preserves publication rights and university IP ownership.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Carlsbergfondet
Criteria: Researchers with strong affiliation to Danish research; basic research in natural sciences, humanities or social sciences
Industrial segment: General, Life Sciences, Chemistry, Physics & Materials, Social Impact
Segment tags: General, Health, Chemistry, Physics, Research, Social Impact
Funding Amount: Varies by instrument (DKK 100K–25M+; e.g. Semper Ardens, postdoc stipends, infrastructure, fieldwork)
Deadline: Efterårsopslag: 1 September (annual); several instruments also rolling
Quick info: Major Danish foundation for free basic research at international level in natural sciences, humanities and social sciences. Efterårsopslag (deadline 1 Sep from 2026) covers Semper Ardens Advance/Accelerate, monograph stipends, research infrastructure, postdoc/reintegration stipends, field expeditions, dissemination (incl. Carlsberg Mindelegat), and more. Rolling schemes include conferences in Denmark, fieldwork under DKK 100K, and acute projects. Apply via CF-Grant.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: NNF Distinguished Innovator Grant
Criteria: Senior Nordic researchers; proven track record
Quick info: Novo Nordisk Foundation grant for senior Nordic researchers with proven track records to pursue high-impact innovation projects. Must act as innovation ambassador within academia. Duration 3 years. TRL 3–5. Mature academic commercialisation by experienced innovators; up to DKK 7.6M / 3 years; pre-CVR.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: NNF Pioneer Innovator Grant
Criteria: Nordic researchers; pre-CVR; health or sustainability focus
Quick info: Primarily supports early-stage research at universities and research institutes (grant to institution, not individual). Themes: cardiometabolic/infectious diseases, agriculture, food, industrial/environmental biotech, carbon capture, quantum tech. Combined annual budget DKK 190M. TRL 1–3. Academic pre-CVR proof-of-concept; up to DKK 1.2M / 1 year.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Open Discovery Innovation Network (ODIN)
Criteria: Precompetitive university-industry collaboration in drug discovery and diagnostics
Quick info: Results openly shared, not patented. DKK 54.5M pilot + DKK 14M from Lundbeck Foundation. TRL low–mid (early discovery). Patent-free open discovery network (universities + industry).
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk
KU contact hint: Preaward RSO (primary). ODIN Secretariat, Aarhus University.

Name: Plant2Food (NNF Open Innovation)
Criteria: Researchers at partner universities (AU, UCPH, DTU, WUR) + industry partners; patent-free open projects
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Food & Agriculture, Cleantech & Energy
Funding Amount: Project grants within platform (Type budgets typically DKK ~1–4M; platform up to DKK 200M)
Deadline: Open calls / rounds (see Plant2Food site; 2026 call published)
Quick info: NNF Open Innovation in Science platform accelerating plant-based foods via patent-free university–industry projects. Hosted at Aarhus University; UCPH is a partner. Results published openly. TRL: low (early-stage / pre-competitive research).
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk
KU contact hint: Preaward RSO (primary). Plant2Food Secretariat, Aarhus University.

Name: BII Early Innovators Grant
Criteria: At least one team member must be a current Bachelor, Master, or PhD student at UCPH, or have graduated from UCPH within the past two years; applicants must be (or become) active KU Lighthouse community members. Early-stage idea with a clear validation plan; company or finished product not required.
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Cleantech & Energy, Deep Tech, Quantum, Tech & AI
Segment tags: Health, Biotech, Cleantech, Sustainability, Deep Tech, Quantum Tech, Tech
Quick info: BioInnovation Institute grant administered by KU Lighthouse. Supports early exploration and validation (prototyping, user research, market assessment, evidence generation). Thematic scope: Human Health, Planetary Health, Societal Resilience, or Quantum (applicant domain need not match). Applications open twice yearly; next call opens 1 September 2026 with deadline 16 October 2026 at 23:59. Independent review panel; recommended applications go to BII for final approval. Selected teams receive onboarding and support through to a project showcase. Not intended for registered businesses with significant funding/traction or as top-up for primary research already funded above DKK 750,000.

Name: DSV Group Innovation Partnerships
Criteria: Logistics automation, sustainability in freight, supply chain digitalisation
Quick info: In-kind access to DSV's global logistics infrastructure for pilot and partnership projects.

Name: Dinero Iværksætterlegat
Criteria: DK company started within last 24 months; CVR required
Quick info: Visma Dinero Iværksætterlegat: 5 × DKK 10,000 once yearly. Applicants must have started a company within the last 24 months and provide CVR plus ownership documentation. Dinero user not required. Max one A4 application page.

Name: EIC Accelerator
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Quantum, Chemistry, Physics & Materials, Deep Tech, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Deep Tech, Health, Cleantech, Chemistry, Physics, Quantum Tech, Materials Science
Deadline: 6 batching dates/year (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov)
Quick info: EU blended finance for single SMEs at TRL 6–8: grant up to €2.5M plus optional equity. Grant-only support available once per company under Horizon Europe. Scale high-risk innovations; grant and/or equity for market deployment.

Name: EIC Pathfinder
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Quantum, Chemistry, Physics & Materials, Deep Tech, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Deep Tech, Health, Cleantech, Chemistry, Physics, Quantum Tech, Materials Science
Quick info: EU programme for ambitious early-stage research consortia pursuing breakthrough science and technology (TRL 1–4). Pathfinder Open and Challenges calls; highly competitive. Total budget EUR 262M. Open call success rate ~2.1% (2025); historically 7–8% (2021–23); Challenges strand typically higher (~10%). Visionary deep-tech research toward radically new technologies.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: ERC Proof of Concept
Criteria: Principal Investigators with an ongoing ERC main grant (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, or Synergy), or a main grant that ended on/after 1 January 2025; proposal must draw substantially on that ERC research.
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Quantum, Chemistry, Physics & Materials, Deep Tech, Cleantech & Energy, Tech & AI
Segment tags: Deep Tech, Health, Cleantech, Chemistry, Physics, Quantum Tech, Materials Science, Tech
Quick info: ERC bridge grant to explore commercial or societal innovation potential of ERC-funded frontier research (testing, validation, IPR/knowledge-transfer strategy, stakeholder engagement). Host institution in EU/Associated Country. One application per call; evaluated on excellence (innovation potential, approach, PI leadership). Grantees may later be eligible pathways toward EIC Transition.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: EIC Transition
Criteria: Must build on eligible prior results (EIC Pathfinder, ERC PoC, Horizon Europe Pillar II RIA, or eligible research infrastructures). Single applicant may be SME/startup/spin-off, university, or research organisation; large companies only in a consortium (2-5 partners).
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Quantum, Chemistry, Physics & Materials, Deep Tech, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Deep Tech, Health, Cleantech, Chemistry, Physics, Quantum Tech, Materials Science
Quick info: EU grant to validate technology in application-relevant settings and develop business/market readiness (typically TRL 3-4 toward 5-6). Universities and RTOs can apply as mono-beneficiary (no company/CVR required at application). Predecessor project must meet eligibility/TRL rules in the EIC Work Programme; technology + business maturation.

Name: EIFO Green Accelerator
Criteria: Danish companies / export alliances with mature green technologies ready for export maturation
Funding Amount: Up to ~EUR 300K / company (de minimis); high co-financing share of eligible costs
Quick info: EIFO grant scheme to mature green export projects (consultancy, market studies, legal/ESG, travel, etc.). Targets proven/export-ready solutions (often described as TRL 9). Company size/export thresholds apply. TRL: 9 (market-ready export maturation).
KU contact hint: KU Lighthouse (for researcher–company cases); applicants are typically companies

Name: EUDP
Quick info: Danish Energy Agency programme for industry-led consortia developing and demonstrating green energy technology (typically TRL 4–8). Co-financing ~40–60%; typical project size DKK 2–15M. 2025 funding DKK 543M.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Eureka
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Chemistry, Physics & Materials, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Quick info: Pan-European network for cross-border R&D collaboration between SMEs. Danish partners can join international consortium projects with national funding through IFD/Eureka national bodies.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Eurostars
Industrial segment: General, Life Sciences, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Quick info: Success rate ~25–30%. IFD funds Danish participants up to EUR 500K if multiple Danish partners.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: GUDP
Quick info: Green Development and Demonstration Programme for food, agriculture, fisheries, and aquaculture. Supports development, demonstration, and network projects with typical grants DKK 250K–15M; ~50% co-financing.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Global Innovation Network Programme (GINP)
Deadline: Final GINP round was 2025; successor international programme via Innovation Fund Denmark (2026–2029 agreement)
Quick info: UFSN programme for international research/innovation networking. 2025 was the fourth and final GINP round; a new IFD-implemented international collaboration programme is planned. Keep for reference / successor watch.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: HeyFunding Legatet
Criteria: DK-based startups; focus on social impact
Quick info: Grant from HeyFunding for early-stage Danish startups with social impact focus. Supports idea validation and early development. Incorporated entity typically needed to receive and deploy grant funds.

Name: Horizon Europe
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Quantum, Chemistry, Physics & Materials, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Tech, Health, Biotech, Cleantech, Sustainability, Chemistry, Physics, Quantum Tech, Materials Science
Quick info: EU flagship R&D programme with rolling topic-specific calls. Danish SMEs and research institutions join collaborative consortia; national contact points and EUopSTART can support proposal preparation.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: IFD Grand Solutions
Industrial segment: General, Life Sciences, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Tech, Health, Biotech, Cleantech, Sustainability, General
Quick info: Main 2026 themes use a two-phase process (Phase 1 expression of interest around early March; Phase 2 full application for invited projects around early/mid September). Separate Defence technology call is one-phase with deadline 1 September 2026. Large consortia addressing major societal challenges. Co-financing: SMEs 35–75%, large companies 25–65%, research institutions up to 90% + overhead. UCPH applicants typically supported via faculty research offices (FRB+ for SCIENCE, Nørre Alle Campus office for SUND). TRL 3–8. Large collaborative high-risk solutions; up to 5 years; universities typically 90% funding rate.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk
KU contact hint: Preaward RSO (primary). Expect FRB+/Nørre routing by faculty for case handling.

Name: IFD Industrial Researcher (Industrial PhD/Postdoc)
Criteria: DK company with CVR employs candidate; university supervisor; company co-finances salary
Industrial segment: General, Life Sciences, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Quick info: IFD funds company–university research hires: Industrial PhD (3 years) or Industrial Postdoc (1–3 years). Company must apply and co-finance; candidate splits time between company and university. Common spin-out route to fund a research employee while retaining academic supervision.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: IFD Innobooster
Criteria: Danish SMEs with CVR number; must have raised DKK 100K or have DKK 250K gross profit
Quick info: Four application windows in 2026 with short pauses between pools (not continuous year-round rolling). Submission date decides which pool you compete in; 2026 windows close 12 Mar, 13 May, 6 Aug, and 15 Oct (12:00). Extension of the Innofounder pathway for incorporated SMEs: co-financing for salaries, external knowledge, equipment, and materials (not rent, transport, or sales/marketing). Eligible costs: salaries, external knowledge providers, equipment, materials. Often used after Innofounder. TRL 4–7. Knowledge-based SME development; max 35% IFD co-financing; up to 24 months.

Name: IFD Innoexplorer
Criteria: Employed at a public Danish research or education institution or hospital; conducts research as part of employment; pre-CVR
Quick info: Assessment: novelty/commercial potential, qualifications, feasibility. UCPH runs an EoI via Lighthouse panel before full application. TRL 3–5. Pre-commercial research-based maturation toward spin-out/start-up; up to 12 months.

Name: IFD Innofounder
Criteria: Higher-ed graduates, early startup; full-time commitment mandatory
Quick info: Non-EU/EEA applicants need Start-up Denmark visa or 1+ year in Denmark. Grant is personal income for tax. CVR required before project start. TRL 1–3. Monthly founder stipend + DKK 100K development grant; 12 months full-time.

Name: Industriens Fond
Criteria: Projects creating positive change for Danish companies (open innovation / competitive calls vary)
Quick info: Private industrial foundation funding original ideas that create change and positive effects for Danish companies. KU Lighthouse can advise on commercially focused applications.

Name: LEO Innovation Lab
Criteria: Start-ups and academic spin-outs in dermatology, digital health, medical devices
Quick info: LEO Pharma's external innovation unit supporting digital health and dermatology startups with pilots, mentorship, and access to LEO Pharma labs and patient registries.

Name: MUDP
Quick info: Ministry of Environment programme co-funding development, test, and demonstration of environmental technology (pre-projects, ETV, dev/demo, and flagship projects). Typical grants DKK 1–4M with ~50% co-financing. 2025 allocation DKK 135M.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Mikrolegat
Criteria: Students in higher ed / recent graduates (3 months) or youth/vocational (Momentum)
Funding Amount: Up to DKK 60K (higher ed); up to DKK 35K (Momentum)
Quick info: Fonden for Entreprenørskab micro-grants for student/pupil ideas. Higher-education Mikrolegat up to DKK 60K; Momentum Mikrolegat for youth/vocational students up to DKK 35K. 25% co-financing if CVR registered.
KU contact hint: KU Lighthouse / Fonden for Entreprenørskab channels

Name: Miljø- og Energi Fonden
Quick info: Private foundation funding Danish environmental and energy innovation projects with grants typically DKK 100K–5M for development and demonstration. Company CVR typically required for project implementation.

Name: NextGen Innovation (Odense Robotics)
Criteria: SMEs with robotics/drone projects in partnership with a knowledge institution
Funding Amount: Up to DKK 350K total (max DKK 200K company + DKK 150K knowledge partner)
Deadline: Per call (check Odense Robotics; Jun 2025 call closed)
Quick info: Odense Robotics / Fyn erhvervsfyrtårn development pool for robot and drone innovation. Requires min. one SME + one knowledge institution. Support is 50% of SME labour costs (de minimis) and 100% for the knowledge partner. Focus areas: large-structure production, advanced drones, autonomous near-coast shipping. Confirm current call status before applying.

Name: Nordic Innovation
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Chemistry, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Quick info: Inter-Nordic organisation funding cross-border innovation projects between Nordic countries. Typical grants €100K–1M for collaborative SME/research partnerships.

Name: Novo Nordisk External Research and Open Innovation
Criteria: Academic spin-outs and start-ups in obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, etc.
Quick info: Novo Nordisk's external innovation partnerships including option-to-licence deals on research collaborations. Deals may include upfront payments and milestones rather than traditional grant funding. Partnership deals usually require an incorporated entity.

Name: Otto Bruuns Fond – Industrielle projekter
Criteria: Inventors, entrepreneurs and smaller companies developing hard-tech industrial inventions or products; realistic business plan preferred
Quick info: Otto Bruuns Fond support for developing industrial inventions and physical products with emphasis on hard tech. Software-only projects rarely supported. Grants mainly cover materials, equipment and concrete development costs. Apply anytime via ottobruunsfond.dk; processed at next board meeting.

Name: Otto Bruuns Fond – Almennyttige projekter
Criteria: Defined activities with general public benefit; typically smaller institutions, NGOs or associations; entrepreneur/inventor industrial development prioritised
Quick info: Otto Bruuns Fond grants for clearly defined projects with general societal benefit. Priority for initiatives that help entrepreneurs and inventors develop industrial inventions. Grant only (no equity). Apply anytime via ottobruunsfond.dk; processed at next board meeting.

Name: Otto Mønsteds Fond – Den Lyse Ide
Criteria: Students and educators at Danish higher-education institutions with an innovative idea
Funding Amount: DKK 500K total across winners (typically 2 prizes + bronze sculptures)
Quick info: Annual Otto Mønsteds Fond prize recognising innovative student/educator ideas with commercial potential for Danish trade and industry. Two winners (Early-stage and Late-stage) share DKK 500K plus bronze sculptures. Nomination via video pitch; winners announced at Digital Tech Summit. Apply 15 April – 15 August.

Name: Otto Mønsteds Fond – Studiemeriterende ophold
Criteria: Engineering students (DTU, AAU, AU, SDU) or business students (CBS, AAU, AU, SDU, RUC); min. 3 months credit-bearing study/internship abroad; GPA ≥ 8
Quick info: Travel grant for merit-bearing study or internship abroad (min. 3 months). Requires pre-approved credit (min. 15 ECTS) and grade average of at least 8. Apply via Otto Mønsteds Fond online portal; decision typically in May. Not open to KU degree programmes under current fund rules.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Otto Mønsteds Fond – Kongresdeltagelse
Criteria: Students, PhD, postdoc or faculty on business/engineering programmes at DTU, CBS, AAU, AU, SDU or RUC; active presenter; congress with commercial/technical focus abroad
Funding Amount: Up to DKK 7,500 (matched to institutional contribution)
Quick info: Supplement for active participation (oral/poster) at international congresses with commercial or technical focus. Max. two grants per five-year period. Host institution must co-fund; fund matches up to DKK 7,500. No support for conferences in Denmark or virtual attendance. Apply via omfonden.dk at least 31 days before departure.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Otto Mønsteds Fond – Forskningsophold
Criteria: PhD, postdoc or faculty on business/engineering programmes at DTU, CBS, AAU, AU, SDU or RUC; min. 3 months abroad; unchanged employment
Funding Amount: Up to DKK 5,000/month (matched to institutional contribution)
Quick info: Monthly supplement for research stays abroad (minimum 3 months) while retaining Danish employment. Max. one stay per five-year period. Covers extra costs abroad only — not ordinary living expenses, family travel, or research materials. Institution must co-fund beyond salary. Apply via omfonden.dk at least 2 months before departure.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Otto Mønsteds Fond – Udenlandske gæsteprofessorater
Criteria: Technical or business faculties at DTU, CBS, AAU, AU, SDU or RUC; institution nominates foreign visiting professors
Funding Amount: Up to DKK 75,000/month (3-month stays; DKK 10M pool in 2026)
Quick info: Institutional scheme to host foreign visiting professors at Danish technical and business faculties. Three-month stays (DKK 75K/month for salary or honorarium). Institution prioritises and nominates candidates; fund selects in autumn. 2026 call: apply Feb–Jun; decisions Oct. KU is not among eligible host universities under current rules.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Otto Mønsteds Fond – Særlige formål
Criteria: Non-profit projects strengthening Danish trade and industry; open to universities, associations and cross-institutional initiatives
Funding Amount: Varies (project-specific; often deficit guarantee for congresses)
Quick info: Broad Otto Mønsteds Fond scheme for projects promoting Danish commerce and industry — e.g. international congresses at Danish universities, entrepreneurship events, student–industry bridges, cross-institutional teaching, and CBS–DTU-style collaborations. Does not fund basic research, product development, or core public-sector tasks. Apply via omfonden.dk; response typically 2–6 months.

Name: Patent og Varemærkestyrelsen
Criteria: DK-based entities; must apply for patent or trademark
Quick info: Danish Patent and Trademark Office subsidies reducing patent and trademark application costs for Danish applicants. Apply when filing IP protection.

Name: Plantefonden (Fonden for Plantebaserede Fødevarer)
Criteria: Projects developing the Danish plant-based food sector (apply via Landbrugs- og Fiskeristyrelsen)
Quick info: Danish fund for plant-based food sector development. Application materials via LFST tilskudsguide. Contact Preaward RSO for SCIENCE/SUND faculty support. Confirm current call before applying.
KU contact email: Frederiksberg: forskningsfinansiering-frbplus@adm.ku.dk | Nørre: forskningsfinansiering-noerre@adm.ku.dk | Søndre: forskningsfinansiering-soendre@adm.ku.dk

Name: Spin-outs Denmark
Stage: Exploratory innovation, Commercial validation, Venture formation
Funding Amount: Up to DKK 600K + bench fee and overhead (1 year)
Quick info: VILLUM-funded national programme for junior researchers commercialising university research. One-year translational postdoc package: funding up to DKK 600K plus bench fee and overhead, with business developer support, mentoring, and pitch training. Department endorsement, written application, and oral pitch required. Applicants apply as researchers, not as a company. TRL low–mid (pre-spin-out).
KU contact hint: KU Lighthouse / tech transfer; Spin-outs Denmark secretariat

Name: UCPH Proof of Concept Fund (POC MAX)
Criteria: UCPH employment required (researcher, postdoc, PhD on staff, or TA); larger commercial initiative
Industrial segment: General, Life Sciences, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Tech, Health, Biotech, Cleantech, Sustainability, General
Quick info: UCPH proof-of-concept fund for researchers validating commercial potential of university discoveries. Duration 12–18 months; funds must be spent within the project period. Grant to UCPH researchers; no company CVR required. TRL 3–9. Up to DKK 500K / 18 months; commercial projects from approved patentable inventions.

Name: UCPH Proof of Concept Fund (POC-TO-GO)
Criteria: UCPH employment required (researcher, postdoc, PhD on staff, or TA); commercial or societal potential
Industrial segment: General, Life Sciences, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Tech, Health, Biotech, Cleantech, Sustainability, General
Quick info: Supported activities: prototype development, IP assessment, market validation, feasibility studies. Grant to UCPH researchers/PhD students; no company CVR required. TRL 1–3. Up to DKK 150K / 6 months; commercial or non-commercial UCPH projects.

Name: Velliv Foreningen
Quick info: Annual grants from Velliv for Danish health, well-being, and social-impact projects. Supports piloting and early development of solutions that improve quality of life.

Name: Villum Foundation and VELUX Group
Criteria: Sustainable building technology, daylight research, indoor climate, biophilic design
Quick info: Joint Villum Foundation–VELUX Group programme (separate from Villum's wider grant portfolio). Collaborative research funding for sustainable building technology, daylight, indoor climate, and biophilic design. VELUX contribution qualifies as co-financing for Innobooster or EUDP.

Name: Vissing Fonden
Criteria: DK energy/climate startup with CVR; active university affiliation; university endorsement required
Quick info: Energy and climate startup grants (typically DKK 200K–300K). CVR and Danish bank account required. At UCPH, energy applications are routed via Lighthouse, which provides the required university endorsement before submission. The fund also runs medical research and children/youth pools — those are not KU Lighthouse support routes.

Name: Copenhagen Health Innovation (CHI)
Criteria: Students + educators matched with Region H clinics/cases
Quick info: Partnership platform (since 2016) connecting students and educators from Copenhagen-area universities/UCCs with hospitals and care organisations on real health-innovation cases. Education-driven collaboration and entrepreneurship skills — not a startup grant programme.

Name: Fonden for Entreprenørskab
Quick info: National foundation for entrepreneurship education in schools and higher education; runs programmes, teacher resources, and student entrepreneurship activities across Denmark.

Name: ITU Business Development
Quick info: IT University of Copenhagen startup programme: co-founder matching, 3-month idea pipeline, and 6-month incubation with mentorship for ITU students.

Name: NOVI Legatet
Quick info: Annual student innovation grant at NOVI science park (North Jutland) supporting entrepreneurship projects by students. Helps student teams test and develop early business ideas.

Name: Novo Nordisk Foundation Fellowship Program Biomedical Design
Criteria: DK-based PhD students; biomedical design focus
Quick info: Fellowship for Danish PhD students in biomedical design; funding and structured training to translate research into health solutions.

Name: ORB
Quick info: Student entrepreneurship organisation (Odense/Aarhus region) supporting young founders with events, mentoring, and innovation activities.

Name: Start Up Factory
Quick info: Aarhus University Engineering Startup Factory — student entrepreneurship programme helping engineering students launch early-stage ventures.

Name: Startup Station
Quick info: Student innovation hub providing workspace, workshops, and mentoring for tech-oriented student founders in Denmark.

Name: Station
Quick info: Copenhagen student innovation hub (tech/design) with co-working, programmes, and community for young founders.

Name: Synapse
Quick info: Student health/biotech innovation community connecting Danish students with life science entrepreneurship programmes and mentors.

Name: UCN Next Step
Quick info: University College Nordjylland entrepreneurship programme for students developing business ideas and early ventures.

Name: BII AI Lab
Criteria: Early-stage AI startup with a clear product hypothesis, a relevant industry application, and potential to build a venture-scale company; technically strong founders with deep domain knowledge
Funding Amount: Programme benefits worth more than DKK 1M; may qualify for pre-seed investment via the AI Fund
Quick info: 12-month venture-building programme across three tracks: AI/Industry, AI/Tech and AI/Deep Tech. Provides tailored venture building, technical infrastructure, industry partners for validating use cases, investor connections and an alumni network.

Name: Scaleup Europe Fund
Criteria: Late-stage/growth companies located in (or relocating to) an EU Member State or a country associated with Horizon Europe Pillar III, developing strategic technologies and raising very large rounds. No open call — the fund manager sources deals
Industrial segment: Life Sciences, Quantum, Deep Tech, Tech & AI, Cleantech & Energy
Segment tags: Deep Tech, Tech, Biotech, Health, Cleantech, Quantum Tech, AI, Energy
Funding Amount: Equity in rounds of ~EUR 100M and above (fund targets ~EUR 5bn)
Deadline: No application route; first investments expected autumn 2026
Quick info: EU late-stage growth equity fund under the EIC Fund umbrella, managed by EQT, with the European Commission, Novo Holdings, EIFO and others as founding investors. There is no application process — EQT sources deals directly. Far beyond researcher or early-founder stage; listed for ecosystem awareness. Watch scaleupeuropefund.eu for updates.

Name: Alexander Foss' Industrifond
Criteria: Danish entrepreneurs; early phase; novel physical product
Quick info: DI-administered foundation (founded 1919) granting stipends to entrepreneurs building technologically innovative physical products. Software-only solutions excluded; not open if you have already raised more than DKK 500K (Innofounder-type soft funding does not count). Funds prototype development, tooling, testing and components. Does not fund patent costs, the founders' own salary, travel or study stays, general operating costs, or expenses already incurred. An optional video pitch can be attached; five to seven grants per year in recent rounds.

Name: Reinholdt W. Jorck og Hustrus Fond
Criteria: Students, graduates or PhDs; 3+ months study/research abroad
Funding Amount: Varies (study/research stay scholarship; amount not published)
Deadline: Annual — 1 August to 15 September; recipients notified mid-December
Quick info: Study- and research-abroad scholarship, not innovation or venture funding. Covers a stay abroad of at least 3 months — part of an ongoing degree, a full degree, or a research stay. Open to technical, commercial, legal, social science or medical fields; grade average of at least 8 and a strong recommendation from a supervisor, professor or recognised expert required. DI does not administer the fund itself; it prioritises and nominates applicants within the technical field. Applications go through the fund's own electronic form.

Name: Karl Pedersen og Hustrus Industrifond
Criteria: Export-strengthening projects; novel; Denmark; company–university partnerships preferred
Funding Amount: Varies (project grants; budget template provided by the fund)
Quick info: DI-administered foundation funding projects that strengthen Danish exports, across three priority areas: new export tools for SMEs, production technology developed jointly by companies and knowledge institutions, and strengthening Danish students' innovation and export skills. Partnerships that do not normally collaborate — e.g. companies with universities, business academies or other knowledge organisations — are explicitly prioritised, which makes this the most KU-relevant of the DI funds. Does not fund single-company profit projects, travel or study stays, or costs already incurred.
